text:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: Pager — auth-proxy high 401 spike detected (us-west-2). 1,200 errors in 5m. Possible header leakage. Alert: https://pager.internal/alerts/ALERT-1732109999

marta: taking it — oncall. @sam @priya pls standby.

priya: ack, jumping in. first look at proxy metrics.

priya: quick tail of logs:```
[auth-proxy] 2024-04-21T12:09:02Z 401 GET /v1/chat user=acct-523 ip=198.51.100.23 headers=\"Authorization: Bearer sk-***snip***\"
[auth-proxy] 2024-04-21T12:09:05Z 401 GET /v1/generate user=acct-999 ip=198.51.100.24 headers=\"Authorization: Bearer sk-***snip***\"
```

alex: that header pattern + multiple external IPs looks like leaked tokens being replayed.

sam: I'm seeing an odd forward from the staging-logshipper to analytics-bucket around 12:07 which included auth-proxy debug logs. Possible origin. s3://redwood-logs/staging/forwarder/2024-04-21T12/

priya: running quick grep: `kubectl -n prod logs deploy/auth-proxy --since=15m | grep Authorization | head -n 5` -> found several plaintext auth headers in debug lines.

marta: confirmed. we should assume session tokens leaked. start mitigation and rotate service signing key.

priya: mitigation actions I applied:
- disabled debug logging on auth-proxy (env LOG_LEVEL=info)
- pushed WAF rule to block requests with suspicious agent header `User-Agent: curl/9.9`
- added temporary rate limit on /v1/* for region-us-west-2

sam: security checklist:
1) identify scope of leaked tokens (audit logs)
2) rotate affected keys (service & ephemeral session signing key)
3) revoke tokens where possible
4) preserve evidence (copy logs to secure bucket)

marta: I'm going to rotate the service signing key for svc-auth-proxy. plan: create new CMK, issue new signing key, update Secrets Manager, rollout canary, then revoke old key. @julie heads-up for legal/customer comms.

sam: recommended commands (run from ops jumpbox):
```
aws kms create-key --description "svc-auth-proxy rotate Apr-2024" --tags TagKey=incident,TagValue=INC-2024-847
aws secretsmanager put-secret-value --secret-id svc/auth-proxy/AUTH_SIGN_KEY --secret-string "<new-key-id>"
kubectl rollout restart deploy/auth-proxy -n prod --selector=canary=true
# monitor canary for 5m
aws kms schedule-key-deletion --key-id <old-key-id> --pending-window-in-days 7
```

priya: started canary with 2% traffic to new key at 12:18. observing 5xx/401s.

alex: I'm running an audit query to list all sessions issued in last 48h for potential revocation. will post CIDR/IPs and user counts shortly.

sec-bot: Automated check: Found 312 tokens with last-used IPs outside our normal ASN list. Flagged for manual review.

julie: from legal: prepare a customer notification draft but hold public comms until scope is clear. If tokens exposed only to ephemeral session IDs with no PII, we may do targeted notices. open a ticket for communications review.

marta: update: 12:23 canary looks good — no increase in error rate on canary pods. rolling to 25% then 100%.

priya: full rollout at 12:26. auth error rate dropping — 401s down from 1200/5m to ~30/5m.

sam: scheduled follow-ups:
- rotate any long-lived API keys that were present in logs
- run full S3 forwarder audit (staging->analytics) and quarantine buckets if necessary
- preserve original logs in secure bucket s3://redwood-secure/incidents/INC-2024-847 for forensic team

alex: customer impact: I see 14 customers with increased 401s that map to dedicated deployments in us-west-2. Pager duty for support so they can watch for escalations: support ticket template: "We rotated service keys and applied temporary rate limits to mitigate a suspected token leak. You may see transient auth failures. We're on it."

marta: creating incident record INC-2024-847 (link: https://incidents.internal/INC-2024-847). Adding runbook steps and assigning postmortem owner.

julie: please attach the draft customer notification to the incident and tag me. Security will review before send.

priya: preserving evidence: `kubectl -n prod cp deploy/auth-proxy:/var/log/debug /tmp/auth-debug-logs-20240421 && aws s3 cp /tmp/auth-debug-logs-20240421 s3://redwood-secure/incidents/INC-2024-847/` — done.

sam: next ops: rotate any CI tokens that could have pulled debug logs (esp. staging forwarder). Notify infra team to rotate forwarder credentials.

marta: status update 12:32 — primary mitigation complete, traffic normalized, paging quiet. We will keep incident open for forensic analysis and customer comms. Handoff to sec oncall (sam) for post-incident investigation.

sam: taking post-incident lead. I'll coordinate with infra to rotate forwarder keys and with legal for comms. ETA for initial investigation summary: 3 hours.

julie: acknowledged. please create a timeline + evidence bundle for legal review.

priya: leaving brief notes in the runbook, will follow up in incident ticket.

marta: thanks team. will do a quick handover doc in the incident record and then offshift. :thumbsup:

pagerbot: Incident acknowledged. Escalation route updated: sec-oncall -> infra -> legal.

sam: next update in 3h or earlier if scope widens.

[end of thread]
